speaker: Doctor

DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignant Ovarian Neoplasm. 

Despite the contradictory reports of "normal" findings in recent imaging and labs, the consistent physical evidence of a large unilateral ovarian mass with significant ascites and a right-sided pleural effusion (Meigs' syndrome presentation or direct metastasis) strongly points to an ovarian malignancy, likely in a 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The negative markers do not rule out serous cystadenocarcinoma or other subtypes.
